This city offers vibrant street life, historic landmarks, and a dazzling food scene. This guide reveals how accessible Mumbai can be.\n\nYou'll learn how to stretch every rupee, avoid common tourist traps, and reach the city's most authentic sights and flavors. With this three-day plan, you'll eat, sleep, and explore for less while soaking up Mumbai's incredible atmosphere.\n\n## Can you really do Mumbai cheap? Yes — here's how\n\nPractical money-saving tactics tailored for thrifty travelers seeking Mumbai's best.\n\nBudget travel in Mumbai is easier than most people expect. Adapt like a local by exploring bustling markets, eating where the crowds gather, and travelling during off-peak hours.\n\nTry staying farther from the main tourist hotspots. Areas like Andheri and Dadar can offer more affordable accommodation, while hostels and guesthouses with breakfast included can add surprising value.\n\nWhen planning your trip, [search flight to Mumbai](https://www.airasia.com/v2/flights/search/?origin=KUL&destination=BOM&departDate=08%2F10%2F2026&tripType=R&adult=1&child=0&infant=0&locale=en-gb&currency=MYR&ule=true&cabinClass=economy&uce=true&ancillaryAbTest=false&isOC=false&isDC=true&returnDate=16%2F10%2F2026&promoCode=&airlineProfile=v%2Cg%2Ck&type=paired) options early to compare fares and find a deal that fits your budget. Booking your [flight to Mumbai](https://www.airasia.com/flights/mumbai-maharashtra/) wisely can leave you with more to spend on exploring the city.\n\nFocus your itinerary on Mumbai's many free cultural experiences. Savour affordable street eats and look for bundle entry rates at paid attractions to stretch your budget further.\n\nCarry a refillable water bottle and use payment apps for transport. These small habits can unlock authentic, low-cost adventures in this electrifying city.\n\n## What a Mumbai trip actually costs (INR + MYR)\n\nA quick visual summary of 2026 travel costs for both backpackers and comfort seekers.\n\n**Key Mumbai budget features (2026):**\n\n- Hostels and guesthouses cost much less in the suburbs, especially Andheri and Dadar\n- Street food meals average just ₹20–₹150 (RM0.90–6.30)\n- Local trains and BEST buses offer massive savings on city transport\n- Three-day total for backpackers is regularly under RM150\n\n**Sample Cost Breakdown:**\n\n|  | Accommodation | Food | Local transport | Sightseeing & extras | Total INR | Total MYR |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Solo backpacker (daily) | ₹600 hostel dorm (6–8 beds) | ₹350 street food/local eatery | ₹50 train/bus | ₹150 free/entry | ₹1,150 | RM49.0 |\n| Mid-range solo (daily) | ₹2,500 budget hotel/private room | ₹1,500 casual restaurant | ₹700 rideshare/taxi | ₹700 paid sights/museums | ₹5,400 | RM230.0 |\n| 3-day solo total | ₹1,800 | ₹1,050 | ₹150 | ₹450 | ₹3,450 | RM146.8 |\n| 3-day couples total | ₹5,000 double room (3 nights) | ₹3,000 (for two people) | ₹2,100 (for two) | ₹2,000 (joint spend) | ₹12,100 | RM515.5 |\n\n- ATM and cash are easiest for small costs; bring small notes for change\n- Confirm rates and exchange before you book, as price shifts are common\n- Sightseeing totals are based on top free landmarks and one paid sight per day\n\nThese numbers reflect real 2026 prices so you can set realistic expectations before arriving and make informed choices for every rupee.\n\n## Where to stay: the 5 budget areas worth comparing\n\nCompare Mumbai's diverse neighborhoods to find the right balance of price, comfort, and connections.\n\n![](https://www.airasia.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1920,quality=75,format=auto/https://rad.airasia.com/assets/0f1fa3c3-e039-4ca7-ac31-4d4c1c5fdcc0)\n\nUrban life near a Mumbai bus stop, Divyanshu Pandey\n\n### Dadar\n\nDadar is a major railway hub with mid-tier accommodation, local Maharashtrian food options, and a central jump-off point for exploring both north and south slices of Mumbai.\n\n## Free and cheap things to do (that are actually worth it)\n\nMumbai's top wallet-friendly experiences that reveal the city's pulse—no expensive tickets required.\n\n![](https://www.airasia.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1920,quality=75,format=auto/https://rad.airasia.com/assets/44be75c3-e366-423e-946b-fc13d707e80b)\n\nGateway of India and Taj Mahal Palace on Mumbai waterfront, Renzo D'souza\n\n### Marine Drive & Gateway of India\n\nEnjoy a free sunset stroll along Marine Drive's Queen's Necklace or snap photos at the iconic Gateway of India. Both are open to all visitors. Early mornings or evenings offer cooler weather and fewer crowds. No entry fee is needed.\n\n## Cheap eats: 5 Mumbai dishes under ₹150 for budget travel in Mumbai\n\nExplore Mumbai's most flavorful meals for less, plus essential safety tips to eat smart and worry-free.\n\n![](https://www.airasia.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1920,quality=75,format=auto/https://rad.airasia.com/assets/d7ef5706-53f9-44e4-9ac2-5c681e3ba3fd)\n\nTraditional vada pav on a ceramic plate, Rahul Sonawane\n\nMumbai is a playground for foodies on a budget. There is much more than vada pav and pav bhaji on offer. Taste masala missal, spicy dabeli, crunchy bhajiyas, or sweet kulfi from local favorite stalls. Most snacks cost between ₹20–₹150 per dish. A bit of variety makes for a full meal. Regional thalis or Iranian bakery treats add unique flavors for adventurous palates.\n\n**Street Food Safety:** Always favor busy stalls with steady customer turnover. Order freshly cooked items and skip raw or pre-cut produce. Bring your own sanitiser. Steer clear of tap water and ask for sealed bottled drinks when in doubt. These habits help you savor Mumbai's culinary wonders without worry.\n\n### Vada pav\n\nMeet the vada pav—Mumbai's signature budget snack. This spiced potato patty comes in a soft bun with tangy chutneys. It's sold throughout the city for just ₹20–₹40. It's filling, fast, and full of flavor. Best enjoyed at bustling train station stalls where turnover guarantees freshness.\n\n### Pav bhaji\n\nPav bhaji is Mumbai's beloved comfort food—a sumptuous veggie mash served with buttery bread rolls. A plate typically costs under ₹150 from local stalls. For a classic taste, visit Sardar Pav Bhaji in Tardeo. Or try sunset servings at Juhu Chowpatty for the quintessential local vibe.\n\n### Dosa & South Indian thali\n\nCrispy dosas and South Indian thali meals bring variety and excellent value to your Mumbai food adventure. Most casual canteens and Udupi restaurants serve these filling vegetarian staples for ₹100–₹200. Away from touristy corners, prices drop even further. Pair a masala dosa with a chai for a complete, cheap lunch.\n\n## Getting around Mumbai without burning cash\n\nInsider insights on navigating Mumbai's top transport modes for the adventurous and budget-minded.\n\n![](https://www.airasia.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1920,quality=75,format=auto/https://rad.airasia.com/assets/0d7a6464-f375-45c8-acd9-88e8d3ff57ce)\n\nAI generated image\n\nMumbai's transport offers more than just savings—it's a city in motion. Riding like a Mumbaikar means getting swept up in that flow. Trains are the city's heartbeat: the click-clack rush, sea breeze at open doors, and new acquaintances swapping tips. The metro provides cool, air-conditioned calm after the city buzz. Airport-to-hotel rides turn sweaty arrivals into smooth ones. Buses are scenic, letting you peer down at street markets and cricket matches en route. Sharing a jam-packed auto with friendly commuters reveals more about the city than any guide. Avoid the morning and evening rush if possible. Embrace a touch of patience—every journey reveals a new side of Mumbai's relentless energy.\n\n### Local trains\n\nMumbai's local trains combine adventure and affordability. Use a Smart Card for multiple rides. Avoid peak times when possible. Hop on at Western, Central, or Harbour lines for speedy city crossings. Just follow the crowds and keep your belongings close.\n\n### Mumbai Metro\n\nMumbai's metro is a cool refuge from city bustle. Buy a Smart Card for regular trips. Check route maps before planning—coverage is expanding but not yet citywide. Metro lines shine for seamless airport connections and quick suburban hops. This makes certain journeys a breeze, especially for first-time travelers.\n\n### BEST buses, auto-rickshaws & ride-hailing\n\nFor routes trains and metro miss, red BEST buses are a Mumbai ritual. Autos zip through suburban traffic. Ride-hailing apps like Uber and Ola are your safety net for late nights or heavy luggage. Fares remain among the lowest for large Asian cities. Confirm your route and price before the journey begins, and enjoy watching Mumbai pass by your window.\n\n## Your 3-day Mumbai budget itinerary\n\nA sample itinerary showing where your money goes—plan smarter, spend less, and see more.\n\n**Key Mumbai budget features (2026):**\n\n- Hostels and guesthouses cost much less in the suburbs, especially Andheri and Dadar\n- Street food meals average just ₹20–₹150 (RM0.90–6.30)\n- Local trains and BEST buses offer massive savings on city transport\n- Three-day total for backpackers is regularly under RM150\n\n**Sample Cost Breakdown:**\n\n|  | Accommodation | Food | Local transport | Sightseeing & extras | Total INR | Total MYR |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Solo backpacker (daily) | ₹600 hostel dorm (6–8 beds) | ₹350 street food/local eatery | ₹50 train/bus | ₹150 free/entry | ₹1,150 | RM49.0 |\n| Mid-range solo (daily) | ₹2,500 budget hotel/private room | ₹1,500 casual restaurant | ₹700 rideshare/taxi | ₹700 paid sights/museums | ₹5,400 | RM230.0 |\n| 3-day solo total | ₹1,800 | ₹1,050 | ₹150 | ₹450 | ₹3,450 | RM146.8 |\n| 3-day couples total | ₹5,000 double room (3 nights) | ₹3,000 (for two people) | ₹2,100 (for two) | ₹2,000 (joint spend) | ₹12,100 | RM515.5 |\n\n- ATM and cash are easiest for small costs; bring small notes for change\n- Confirm rates and exchange before you book, as price shifts are common\n- Sightseeing totals are based on top free landmarks and one paid sight per day\n\nThese numbers reflect real 2026 prices so you can set realistic expectations before arriving and make informed choices for every rupee.\n\nTips: Book your [hotels in Mumbai](https://www.airasia.com/hotel/search?currency=MYR&country_code=my&checkin=2026-11-14&checkout=2026-11-21&occupancy=2&location_id=657&languageId=en-gb) in advance to enjoy cheaper rates!\n\n## How to save money & when to go for budget travel in Mumbai\n\nSeasonal Mumbai tips and tricks to stretch your rupees further—timing and habits matter.\n\n**Key Mumbai budget features (2026):**\n\n- Hostels and guesthouses cost much less in the suburbs, especially Andheri and Dadar\n- Street food meals average just ₹20–₹150 (RM0.90–6.30)\n- Local trains and BEST buses offer massive savings on city transport\n- Three-day total for backpackers is regularly under RM150\n\n**Sample Cost Breakdown:**\n\n|  | Accommodation | Food | Local transport | Sightseeing & extras | Total INR | Total MYR |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| Solo backpacker (daily) | ₹600 hostel dorm (6–8 beds) | ₹350 street food/local eatery | ₹50 train/bus | ₹150 free/entry | ₹1,150 | RM49.0 |\n| Mid-range solo (daily) | ₹2,500 budget hotel/private room | ₹1,500 casual restaurant | ₹700 rideshare/taxi | ₹700 paid sights/museums | ₹5,400 | RM230.0 |\n| 3-day solo total | ₹1,800 | ₹1,050 | ₹150 | ₹450 | ₹3,450 | RM146.8 |\n| 3-day couples total | ₹5,000 double room (3 nights) | ₹3,000 (for two people) | ₹2,100 (for two) | ₹2,000 (joint spend) | ₹12,100 | RM515.5 |\n\n- ATM and cash are easiest for small costs; bring small notes for change\n- Confirm rates and exchange before you book, as price shifts are common\n- Sightseeing totals are based on top free landmarks and one paid sight per day\n\nThese numbers reflect real 2026 prices so you can set realistic expectations before arriving and make informed choices for every rupee.\n\nTips: Book your [hotels in Mumbai](https://www.airasia.com/hotel/search?currency=MYR&country_code=my&checkin=2026-11-14&checkout=2026-11-21&occupancy=2&location_id=657&languageId=en-gb) in advance to enjoy cheaper rates!\n\n## Mumbai tips specifically for Malaysian travellers\n\n[Book Now](https://www.airasia.com/flights)\n\nA focused cheat-sheet for Malaysian visitors—visa, money, SIM, flights, and halal-friendly spots.\n\nIf you're traveling from Malaysia, begin your Mumbai planning with the India e-Visa process (usually 3–5 days online). For money, use ATMs in city centers for rupees and carry plenty of small notes for markets and street food.\n\nMulti-currency cards like Wise or Revolut offer good rates for larger purchases, though smaller vendors prefer cash. At the airport, SIM cards from Airtel or Jio (available with passport/visa) ensure instant connectivity. Get one at arrivals for the smoothest start.\n\nFor food, vegetarian options are everywhere. Halal-friendly restaurants are found in Bandra, Mohammed Ali Road, and Bhendi Bazaar. Getting from the airport to the city is easy: prepaid taxis, Uber/Ola, or the metro will get you downtown in 30–90 minutes depending on traffic.\n\nAlways compare [KUL–BOM flight options](https://www.airasia.com/flights/from-kuala-lumpur-kul-to-mumbai-bom/) before purchasing. Better deals mean more funds for Mumbai's endless tastes and experiences.\n\nYou may also explore our guides on [8 Film Locations in Mumbai for Bollywood Movie Buffs](https://www.airasia.com/blog/india/mumbai/bollywood-film-locations/) and [India Travel Guide 2026: Best Places, Itineraries, Visa Tips & Travel Essentials](https://www.airasia.com/blog/india/india-travel-guide/) for more travel inspiration.\n\n[Book Now](https://www.airasia.com/flights)\n\n## Ready to plan your Mumbai trip?\n\n[Book Now](https://www.airasia.com/v2/flights/search/?origin=KUL&destination=BOM&departDate=08%2F10%2F2026&tripType=R&adult=1&child=0&infant=0&locale=en-gb&currency=MYR&ule=true&cabinClass=economy&uce=true&ancillaryAbTest=false&isOC=false&isDC=true&returnDate=16%2F10%2F2026&promoCode=&airlineProfile=v%2Cg%2Ck&type=paired)\n\nStep-by-step prep for your budget Mumbai adventure—make your funds, time, and excitement go further.\n\nBegin your budget travel in Mumbai by comparing KUL–BOM flights. There are 1–2 nonstop options each day, so flexible dates can mean big savings. Choose your accommodation strategically. Nightlife and sightseeing fans love Colaba and Fort. Transport-savvy travelers opt for Andheri or Dadar for swift airport and rail links. Always filter hotels for flexible cancellation policies and cross-check terms before confirming. Keep your curated 3-day itinerary handy—it will save you time and money as you navigate Mumbai's ceaseless activity. Trust the energy of a crowded food stall for discovering top street eats. Mumbai rewards those who travel smart and with curiosity.\n\n[Book Now](https://www.airasia.com/v2/flights/search/?origin=KUL&destination=BOM&departDate=08%2F10%2F2026&tripType=R&adult=1&child=0&infant=0&locale=en-gb&currency=MYR&ule=true&cabinClass=economy&uce=true&ancillaryAbTest=false&isOC=false&isDC=true&returnDate=16%2F10%2F2026&promoCode=&airlineProfile=v%2Cg%2Ck&type=paired)\n\n## FAQs: Mumbai budget travel questions answered\n\nYour top Mumbai travel questions, deconstructed for maximum clarity—dispel myths and discover hidden details.\n\n### 1\\. Is Mumbai cheap to visit?\n\nYes, Mumbai remains a highly affordable destination for budget travel in Mumbai. Leverage local meals, suburban public transport, and off-peak hotel deals. Costs rise quickly in tourist hotspots and imported goods shops—embrace local choices for real savings.\n\n### 2\\. How much does Mumbai cost per day?\n\nActual daily costs depend on your style. Live like a local—street eats, trains, hostels—for INR 1,500–2,000 per day. Those seeking more privacy and comfort should budget INR 2,500–5,000 or more. For higher-end experiences, adjust your budget accordingly. 2026 prices continue to track with broader city trends.\n\n### 3\\. Can I visit Mumbai with RM1,000?\n\nRM1,000 usually stretches to 3–4 days of tight-budget travel. This works especially well if you snack from hawker carts and use local transit. For comfort upgrades or shopping sprees, give yourself extra funds. A little strategic planning unlocks surprisingly rich experiences on modest sums.\n\n### 4\\. Is Mumbai cheaper than Delhi?\n\nLocal food and transport are comparable in Mumbai and Delhi. Mumbai generally has pricier accommodation for central locations. However, unique free sights and waterfront experiences help offset the cost difference between the two iconic cities.\n\n### 5\\. What's the cheapest area to stay?\n\nAndheri and Dadar consistently offer the best value for accommodation. Andheri features lower prices at the cost of longer travel. Dadar provides a balanced location but can book up quickly. Consider reviews and proximity to train stations for optimal savings.\n\n### 6\\. How much does food cost?\n\nIconic Mumbai snacks can cost as little as INR 20–150 each. Sit-down local meals run INR 200–400 per person. Mid-range restaurants are higher, but budget diners and hawker stalls ensure you can eat well and spend little. Choose locations with high turnover and fresh food for the best experience.\n\n![Phaksornkan T.](https://www.airasia.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1920,quality=75,format=auto/https://rad.airasia.com/assets/2dfc67ac-7c52-416e-a503-d50b85cd5472)\n\n#### Phaksornkan T.\n\n25 September 2026\n\nFueled by good coffee, iced matcha, and post-travel Pilates, I’m constantly on the hunt for the next great cafe and destination. Please try a different city name/boarding point.\n\n## Online Bus Tickets Booking with IntrCity SmartBus\n\n![Bus](https://images.railyatri.in/ry_images_prod/busbg-1-1771839365.png)\n\nBook bus tickets online with IntrCity SmartBus and enjoy complete control over your journey, from choosing your perfect seat to leaving on time and tracking your bus in real time. Unlike marketplaces, IntrCity operates and manages its own fleet, ensuring safer, cleaner and more reliable intercity travel. IntrCity SmartBus is India’s largest intercity bus operator, offering safe, reliable and well-managed online bus booking across major cities and routes in India. Unlike aggregator platforms, we operate a large branded smart bus fleet to ensure consistent service quality, punctual departures and a premium bus travel experience on every journey.\n\nAfter you book, you receive clear notifications with your boarding point details, including an exact location pin and landmark. On the day of departure, our staff or captain is present at the verified boarding point to assist with check-in, answer questions, and help with luggage. Once your bus starts its journey, you can track its exact location using our app or website. This helps you estimate arrival time, reduce waiting at boarding points and stay informed about any traffic-related delays. The live GPS ensures transparency and enhances journey planning for both passengers and their families.\n\n![Live Tracking Icon](https://images.railyatri.in/ry_images_prod/trackicon-1773604381.png)\n\nLIVE GPS Tracking\n\n800+Routes Covered\n\n200+Cities Connected\n\n2000+Active Buses\n\n5000+Daily Trips\n\n### How to Track Your Bus\n\n1\n\n#### Open the IntrCity App or visit the official website.\n\nDownload the IntrCity SmartBus app on iOS or Android, or use the tracking feature directly on the website.\n\n2\n\n#### Enter your mobile number or PNR number.\n\nUse the mobile number linked to your booking or your booking PNR to instantly access your trip's live location.\n\n✅\n\nWith just these two simple steps, you can access real-time [bus tracking](https://www.intrcity.com/live-bus-tracking) information, and you will also receive notifications via the app regarding arrival times and potential delays.\n\n* * *\n\n### Extra Assistance Features\n\n![Alarm Icon](https://images.railyatri.in/ry_images_prod/alarmiconMin-1773642061.png)\n\nWake-up Call / Alarm Before Departure\n\nPassengers can opt for a wake-up reminder before departure to avoid missing their bus. This feature sends timely alerts before boarding time, helping travellers stay prepared and on time for their journey.\n\n![Lost/Found Icon](https://images.railyatri.in/ry_images_prod/lostfoundicon-1773642051.png)\n\nLost & Found Assistance\n\nIf any personal belongings are misplaced during the journey, we assist in coordinating with the operations team to help recover items whenever possible.\n\n## Private Bus Booking for Group and Corporate Travel\n\nPlan your next corporate offsite, team outing, or group event without the usual rental hassles. Private bus booking is ideal for corporate travel, group trips, weddings, school excursions, religious tours, and outstation events where booking individual seats is impractical. With IntrCity, you get professionally managed buses operated by trained drivers, verified routes, and consistent service quality across cities. Whether you need a sleeper bus for overnight group travel or an AC seater for short-distance travel, you can choose the right vehicle size and configuration for your needs.         "title": "BEST trims fares of bus passes, to benefit students, senior citizens",
        "description": "# Mumbai: BEST trims fares of bus passes, to benefit students, senior citizens\n- **Text Size**\n\n[Print](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshowprint/99280150.cms)\n\n![Mumbai: BEST trims fares of bus passes, to benefit students, senior citizens](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-99280184,imgsize-2459664,width-400,height-225,resizemode-75/best-bus.jpg)\n\nBased on passenger feedback, BEST has also discontinued plans that have not seen enough adoption. The new plans will come into effect from Friday. (File photo)\n\nMUMBAI: The BEST on Wednesday announced new, simplified bus passes with lower fares for office-goers, students and senior citizens - with all plans now allowing travel in both AC and non-AC buses. Apart from offering convenience, the new plans also help commuters save up to 60% when compared to buying daily tickets, said BEST general manager Lokesh Chandra.He said this has been done to make digital tickets more attractive for Mumbaikars. Updates have been made to the Super Saver Plans, student passes, unlimited rides passes and senior citizens passes. \"Now, passengers can travel on both AC and Non-AC buses with any plan,\" he said.Based on passenger feedback, BEST has also discontinued plans that have not seen enough adoption. The new plans will come into effect from Friday.Super Saver Plans - The plans in the Rs 6 fare slab are cheaper. For example, one can purchase a Rs 219 pass for 28 days and get 60 trips, while one can make four trips each worth Rs 6 ticket in a day for just Rs 15 daily bus pass (which comes to less than Rs 4 per trip). Unlimited Rides Passes - Price of the unlimited rides AC pass will be reduced from Rs 60 to Rs 50 for the single-day pass and from Rs 1,250 to Rs 750 for the monthly pass to encourage more passengers to avail its benefit.\n\nStudent Pass - A simple, single 30-day student pass will be introduced for private school and college students, offering 60 trips for just Rs 200 (introductory offer). Senior Citizen Pass - Senior citizens will be entitled to a flat Rs.50 discount on all Super Saver Plans of 28 days and longer. The plans can be purchased both on the BEST Chalo app and the BEST Chalo card. Select the plan of your choice, enter your details and make an online payment via UPI, debit or credit card, net banking etc. to purchase the plan, Chandra added. BEST Chalo card users can get the new plans loaded on the card through the conductor and simply tap to pay for their travel.\n\n**You Can Also Check: [Gold Rate in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/gold-rates-today/gold-price-in-mumbai) | [Silver Rate in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/silver-rates-today/silver-price-in-mumbai) | [Bank Holidays in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/bank-holidays/maharashtra) | [Public Holidays in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/public-holidays/maharashtra) | [Mumbai AQI](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/weather/mumbai-aqi-level-air-quality-index-today/3258) | [Weather in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/weather/mumbai-weather-forecast-today/3258) | [Petrol Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/petrol-price/petrol-price-in-mumbai) | [Diesel Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/diesel-price/diesel-price-in-mumbai) | [CNG Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/cng-price/cng-price-in-mumbai) | [LPG Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/lpg-price/lpg-price-in-mumbai)**\n\n[Stay updated with the latest Mumbai news.         "markdown": "Sun, Oct 18, 2026 \\| Updated 06.52PM IST\n\n[Weather](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/weather)\n\n[![TOI logo](https://static.toiimg.com/photo/92222747.cms)](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/)\n\nSign In\n\nThis story is from April 06, 2023\n\n# Mumbai: BEST trims fares of bus passes, to benefit students, senior citizens\n\n[![](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/authorphoto/1349.cms)](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-Somit-Sen-1349.cms)[Somit Sen](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/toireporter/author-Somit-Sen-1349.cms) / TNN / Updated: Apr 06, 2023, 04:32 IST\n\nSave\n\nComments\n\nShare\n\nAa\n\n+ **Text Size**\n\n- Small\n- Medium\n- Large\n\n[Print](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/articleshowprint/99280150.cms \"print article\")\n\n![Mumbai: BEST trims fares of bus passes, to benefit students, senior citizens](https://static.toiimg.com/thumb/msid-99280184,imgsize-2459664,width-400,height-225,resizemode-75/best-bus.jpg)\n\nBased on passenger feedback, BEST has also discontinued plans that have not seen enough adoption. The new plans will come into effect from Friday. (File photo)\n\nMUMBAI: The BEST on Wednesday announced new, simplified bus passes with lower fares for office-goers, students and senior citizens - with all plans now allowing travel in both AC and non-AC buses. Apart from offering convenience, the new plans also help commuters save up to 60% when compared to buying daily tickets, said BEST general manager Lokesh Chandra.He said this has been done to make digital tickets more attractive for Mumbaikars. Updates have been made to the Super Saver Plans, student passes, unlimited rides passes and senior citizens passes. \"Now, passengers can travel on both AC and Non-AC buses with any plan,\" he said.Based on passenger feedback, BEST has also discontinued plans that have not seen enough adoption. The new plans will come into effect from Friday.Super Saver Plans - The plans in the Rs 6 fare slab are cheaper. For example, one can purchase a Rs 219 pass for 28 days and get 60 trips, while one can make four trips each worth Rs 6 ticket in a day for just Rs 15 daily bus pass (which comes to less than Rs 4 per trip).Unlimited Rides Passes - Price of the unlimited rides AC pass will be reduced from Rs 60 to Rs 50 for the single-day pass and from Rs 1,250 to Rs 750 for the monthly pass to encourage more passengers to avail its benefit.\n\nStudent Pass - A simple, single 30-day student pass will be introduced for private school and college students, offering 60 trips for just Rs 200 (introductory offer).Senior Citizen Pass - Senior citizens will be entitled to a flat Rs.50 discount on all Super Saver Plans of 28 days and longer. The plans can be purchased both on the BEST Chalo app and the BEST Chalo card. Select the plan of your choice, enter your details and make an online payment via UPI, debit or credit card, net banking etc. to purchase the plan, Chandra added. BEST Chalo card users can get the new plans loaded on the card through the conductor and simply tap to pay for their travel.\n\n**You Can Also Check: [Gold Rate in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/gold-rates-today/gold-price-in-mumbai) \\| [Silver Rate in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/silver-rates-today/silver-price-in-mumbai) \\| [Bank Holidays in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/bank-holidays/maharashtra) \\| [Public Holidays in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/public-holidays/maharashtra) \\| [Mumbai AQI](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/weather/mumbai-aqi-level-air-quality-index-today/3258) \\| [Weather in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/weather/mumbai-weather-forecast-today/3258) \\| [Petrol Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/petrol-price/petrol-price-in-mumbai) \\| [Diesel Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/diesel-price/diesel-price-in-mumbai) \\| [CNG Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/cng-price/cng-price-in-mumbai) \\| [LPG Price in Mumbai](https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/fuel-price/lpg-price/lpg-price-in-mumbai)**\n\n[Stay updated with the latest Mumbai news.
